title: What would happen if a major bridge closed during rush hour?
sources: Federal Highway Administration Traffic Flow Theory

lines.text: What happens to an entire metropolitan city when a critical suspension bridge suddenly shuts down at 5 PM?
lines.caps: What happens when a *bridge | shuts down in rush *hour?

lines.text: Modern highway networks function like complex hydraulic systems under extreme pressure.
When a bridge carrying one hundred thousand cars daily closes, traffic doesn't just stop; it detonates backwards.
lines.caps: Closing a bridge *detonates | traffic backwards for *miles!

lines.text: GPS navigation algorithms frantically reroute tens of thousands of vehicles onto narrow suburban side streets.
lines.caps: GPS reroutes *thousands of cars | into narrow *neighborhoods

lines.text: Neighborhood roads gridlock instantly, trapping emergency ambulances, fire trucks, and city buses.
A single point of failure can paralyze an entire metro economy for twenty straight miles.
It proves just how dependent our cities are on a handful of steel and concrete arteries.
lines.caps: Cities rely on a *few critical | concrete *arteries!
